---
title: Extending
guide-section: Development
---

## Add an app

1. Add `src/ha_automations/apps/<name>.py` with a `Config` subclass for its settings, giving every field a `Field(description=...)`, and an AppDaemon app class that validates its args with it. Keep logic that does not need Home Assistant in its own module so it can be tested with fakes. See `light_fade.py` and `fades.py`.
2. Add the shim `deploy/appdaemon/apps/<name>.py`, importing the app class.
3. Add tests under `tests/`.
4. Add `docs/apps/<name>.qmd`, rendering its settings table with the `_helpers.py` functions. Add the app to `docs/apps/index.qmd` and the homepage.

### A light fade app

For a light fade with other defaults, add a `LightFadeSettings` subclass for the defaults and a `LightFadeApp` subclass that sets `Settings` to it. Give every overridden field a `Field(description=...)`. See `sunset_fade.py`. Add it to the parametrized tests in `tests/test_apps.py`, and follow `sunset-fade.qmd` for its page, which adds a chart.

## Add a detector

1. Add `src/ha_automations/detectors/<name>.py` with a class that has `read()` and `listen()`, and a `Config` model with `kind: Literal["<name>"]` and a `build(app)` method. See `sun.py`.
2. Make `DetectorConfig` in `detectors/__init__.py` a union discriminated on `kind`.

## Add a trigger

1. Add a `Config` model with a `listen(app, callback)` method to `triggers.py`.
2. Add it to the `TriggerConfig` union.
3. Add it to the triggers table on the Light Fade page.
